narratives.Overview:
## Problem

Three open Dependabot alerts on the same transitive pin brace-expansion @ 5.0.9 (runtime via minimatch@10). Prior pin brace-expansion@5: 5.0.9 from #4348 / alerts #10/#13 is short of this trio.

| Alert | Severity | Advisory | CVE | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [#16](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/dependabot/16) | HIGH | GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p | CVE-2026-102276 | >= 5.0.10 (parseCommaParts stack DoS) |
| [#17](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/dependabot/17) | HIGH | GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7 | CVE-2026-102278 | >= 5.0.11 (nested brace-group stack DoS) |
| [#18](https://github.com/deftai/directive/security/dependabot/18) | MEDIUM | GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr | CVE-2026-102277 | **5.0.12** (quadratic {a},b} CPU DoS) |

Distinct from the earlier CVE-2026-14257 / GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg tail-recursion fix. One pin to **5.0.12** clears all three.

Dedup: this issue is the ship vehicle. #5738 and #5739 close as duplicates of this one.

## What to build

Bump the pnpm 11 workspace override for brace-expansion@5 to **5.0.12**, refresh pnpm-lock.yaml, and record the pin in CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

## Acceptance

- [ ] pnpm-workspace.yaml pins brace-expansion@5 to **5.0.12**.
- [ ] pnpm-lock.yaml resolves brace-expansion@5 to 5.0.12 (out of all three vulnerable ranges).
- [ ] CHANGELOG [Unreleased] records the bump and cites Dependabot #16/#17/#18.
- [ ] Dependabot alerts #16, #17, and #18 auto-close or are dismissable as fixed.

Literal check:


pnpm why brace-expansion


## Related

- Duplicate of this ship: #5738, #5739
- Prior pin: #4348

Prefer-A survives refutation: no blocks-the-design finding. I read the issue body and the three specified comments, with no post-ceiling thread input. Verification used git show at the dispatch SHA plus read-only REST retrieval of Dependabot alerts 16/17/18; no installation, product edits, or exploit execution.

Existing mechanisms: pnpm-workspace.yaml already has major-scoped overrides and exact-version minimumReleaseAgeExclude entries. The pinned lockfile contains the 5.0.9 override, package resolution/integrity, snapshot, and minimatch@10.2.5 dependency edge to 5.0.9. Its brace-expansion search found no resolved 2.x package. package.json pins pnpm@11.8.0. These mechanisms support the proposed narrow update; a new override mechanism is unnecessary.

### F1 — sharpens-framing: distinguish the patched boundary from proof of completed remediation
Evidence: live alert records independently report first patched versions 5.0.10, 5.0.11, and 5.0.12 respectively. Thus 5.0.12 is sufficient for these recorded ranges; Stop 1's phrase "past 5.0.12" is stricter than the actual boundary. The pinned lockfile shows that updating the override text alone would leave a vulnerable minimatch edge and package snapshot unless the refresh succeeds.
Failure mode: interpreting "past" literally rejects the intended exact pin, while treating the intended bump as proof that alerts have cleared overstates a proposed change before the resulting graph and GitHub scan exist.
Disposition consequence: the lean can bind with an exact 5.0.12 target and an explicit verification statement: regenerate with the pinned pnpm version, confirm every resolved 5.x brace-expansion node/edge is 5.0.12 and no 5.0.9 resolution survives, validate a frozen-lockfile install, and inspect workspace-wide dependency paths (pnpm -r why brace-expansion). Record GitHub alert closure separately after the default-branch dependency scan; until then say the lockfile is outside the recorded vulnerable ranges, not that closure was observed. This uses existing package-manager checks and keeps the three-file scope.

### F2 — footnote: retaining the 2.1.4 override is scoped deferral, not evidence that both major lines are patched
Evidence: the existing workspace override/comment still describes both major lines as patched, but alert advisory data also lists affected 2.x ranges, with 2.1.7 the highest first-patched 2.x version across this trio. No 2.x resolution appears in the dispatch lockfile.
Failure mode: a future dependency introducing major 2 would be forced onto the vulnerable 2.1.4 pin; a blanket claim that all brace-expansion lines are secured would therefore be false. This is a latent dependency-policy risk, not evidence of a second currently resolved vulnerable path.
Disposition consequence: no scope expansion required for P1. Keep the current 2.x keep-out and limit release-note/security claims to the resolved 5.x path and alerts 16/17/18. A newly resolved 2.x node would be the evidence that changes this disposition.

The untrusted-input failure here is availability loss through glob parsing: the advisories explain why output-count/length limits do not prevent these parsing failures. Keeping 5.0.9 and relying on those limits is therefore not an equivalent remedy. Partial bumps to 5.0.10 or 5.0.11 also leave a recorded advisory range open. No new prompt-authority or concurrent-worker mechanism is introduced by this dependency pin change.
